# Working of Fibonacci Series

#### Course: Learn Recursion With C++

## Working of Fibonacci Series

We now know that the sequence of function calls in the Fibonacci series is not linear but rather resembles a tree.

But function calls/returns still take place sequentially, one after the other.

Consider the return statement below:

```cpp
return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2);
```

Here, fib(num - 2) comes after fib(num - 1). So, fib(num - 2) is evaluated only after fib(num - 1) returns a value.

![Order of Evaluation in Recursion](data:image/png;base64,)

So, the left-hand side must return a value first before calling the function on the right-hand side.

The order in which the calls and returns occur is shown in the figure below.

![Order of Evaluation in the fib() Function](data:image/png;base64,)
